method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the 'Poliomyelitis' chapter of the Australian Immunisation Handbook, retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the Stroke Foundation, Kidney Health Australia and NHFA/CSANZ sources already in this compendium.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Children: 4 doses of IPV-containing vaccine at 2, 4 and 6 months and 4 years** — **not at 18 months**, unlike DTPa and Hib. **First dose from 6 weeks.**
claims.source_text: Inactivated poliovirus (IPV)-containing vaccine is recommended for infants and children in a 4-dose schedule at 2, 4 and 6 months and 4 years of age. Infants can have their 1st dose of IPV-containing vaccine as early as 6 weeks of age.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Poliomyelitis', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/poliomyelitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Travellers to areas or countries with polio cases: an IPV booster every 10 years.**
claims.source_text: Travellers to areas or countries where people are infected with polio 1 are recommended to receive a booster dose of inactivated poliovirus (IPV) vaccine or an IPV-containing vaccine every 10 years.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Poliomyelitis', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/poliomyelitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Polio is notifiable in every state and territory.**
claims.source_text: notifiable disease in all states and territories in Australia.
